event: Someone knocks on the warehouse door, and Callum does not receive visitors.
He sets down his soldering wand; all three threads run steady, and Danger Sense shows no threat.
Three sharp raps again, from someone used to doors opening the first time.
He crosses past the Refinery, the cot, and the Enhancement Construct at 75%, and opens the door.
Mira Vasquez stands in the gray afternoon light with her arms crossed.
Five-seven and lean, in worn leather armor, her saber's cord grip worn smooth with use.
"You're hard to find." "I'm not hiding." Not in the doorway, she says; he steps aside.
She circles the Refinery without touching it and stops at the Grinder's relay.
She asked around the Exchange: everyone knows him as the quiet one who never haggles right.
He paid forty-five Gold a fragment last week, she says; the market rate was forty-two.
At the workbench she asks what the Enhancement Construct does.
It feeds the Refinery's output back into the others as upgrades, he says, so the chain compounds.
"It makes them feed each other," Mira says. "That's not how anyone thinks about this."
She asks about Pip. "Compiled Familiar. His name is Pip." It doesn't talk.
Pacing, she lays out her problem: Level 23 Sword Saint, half a level a week on eight hours a day.
He supplies the numbers: 4,363 XP to Level 25, about 620 XP a day at her kill rate.
He worked it out from one fight. "I calculate everything. It's what I do."
Active play doesn't scale, she says; Summoners and Aura Knights idle past her while they sleep.
Near him two days ago her interface felt a tailwind: faster attacks, shorter cooldowns.
The aura is bleeding into nearby players, he admits, and he doesn't fully understand why.
She wants sustained access to the effect, a baseline to build a training rhythm around.
In return she'll protect his operation: sweeps twice a day, the warehouse as her base.
And when he can, he'll help with her Condense, a reset her class can't survive alone.
He can't solve it yet; she isn't asking for a solution today, only the commitment.
The calculation says yes; beneath it, she is a person who chose to trust him first.
"Deal." Her handshake is callused and sure.
She'll run the first sweep this evening and needs somewhere to sleep; he has one cot.
"I'll get another one." She'll be back in two hours with her gear.
At the door: his constructs fight like drunk toddlers, but the operation is something else.
"That just happened," he tells Pip.
Late in the afternoon he carries forty-seven Flux Capacitor components into the Exchange.
His usual buyer is Harlow, a construct-smith who supplies mid-tier workshops.
Harlow counts forty-seven, cleaner than the Guild processors' work. "You heard about the tax?"
The Vanguard pushed it through the Compact council this morning: unaffiliated owe fifteen percent.
It was five percent; enforcers are already posting rate cards at the gate stations.
He works it out: the Enhancement Construct slips from five days away to twelve.
He asks 705 for the batch; Harlow, apologetic, must withhold the tax at the point of sale.
Net 600 Gold, 105 lost to a political decision. His balance reads 1,847.

changes.note: Sale nets 600 Gold; 1,847 stated, so 7 Gold of income came in unstated since chapter 1

event: Turning away, he nearly walks into two Vanguard enforcers posting the new rate card.
Unaffiliated traders protest; an enforcer answers with polite finality and a sword behind it.
A potion seller shutters early; a gatherer he knows from the north ruins recounts his coins.
He files it: Drake Morrison is costing him compound interest, and doesn't know he exists.
He walks home through streets that feel slightly narrower than they did that morning.
Two hours after she left, Mira returns with a canvas duffel and her saber.
Bedroll, spare clothes, whetstone, ration bars, rope, and a water-damaged fencing manual.
She asks where the second cot is. "Floor's fine." She wants the deployment zones.
He maps Loop Sight in his notebook: Sentinel on the Overgrowth edge, Collector north, Grinder east.
Blind spots: a forty-minute gap to the southwest, and a weak thirty-meter relay stretch.
She'll sweep those morning and evening; anything she can't handle, she falls back here.
"You rehearsed that." His plans had a blank slot for a combat person. "You're a weird guy."
With her covering the gaps, the Sentinel can retreat at 20% instead of 30%: about 8% more kills.
He catches himself valuing her as output. She is a person. Both things can be true.
Evening: on her bedroll Mira sharpens the Fracture-Tooth Saber, shk, shk, shk.
He has stared at his notebook for twenty minutes; she says he hasn't blinked convincingly.
She tosses him a ration bar; it bounces off his palm and he snatches it off the cot.
They eat in silence. Does he talk to Pip? "It doesn't talk back." "That tracks."
The silence turns shaped: two people who have agreed to share a space.
She asks how bad the tax is: twelve days to the construct, and about forty Gold a week lost.
Barrier costs haven't changed in two months, he says; this is revenue extraction.
Drake offered her a Vanguard spot three months ago, and she turned him down: she takes no orders.
Can he sell more? He's at full Refinery throughput; the bottleneck is materials.
She offers to clear a Tier 2 salvage corridor south of the Foundry District for his Collector.
Better scrap lifts components from 15 Gold to about 19; twelve days becomes eight.
"Still not five." "No. But eight is better than twelve." She'll clear it on tomorrow's sweep.
She settles against the wall; a new thread has entered the loop, in a colour he can't name.
Enhancement Construct: eight days. Sweeps: twice daily. Aura: unmeasured. Partnership: initiated.
He listens to her breathing slow into sleep beside the constructs' endless loops.
The curve is still bending, and he is no longer the only one watching it.
